## 4. Route I: nonlinear chronological propagation under a siphon condition
A nonempty species set Z is a siphon if every reaction with a product in Z has a reactant in Z. Assume additionally:
**(SC)** For every siphon Z there is a nonzero w_Z≥0 with support contained in Z and w_Z·Delta_e=0 for every reaction e.
It is enough to check minimal siphons. On the fixed positive class let m_Z=w_Z·c>0. There are finitely many Z; choose

If there are no siphons, use epsilon=1. At any starting state x(s)∈P, put J_0={i:x_i(s)≥epsilon}. Its complement cannot contain a siphon: otherwise the conserved m_Z would be strictly less than epsilon||w_Z||_1≤m_Z/2. Starting from J_0, repeatedly add every product species of a reaction all of whose reactants already belong to J_r. If a nonempty complement remains when this process stops, that complement is a siphon, a contradiction. Therefore the closure contains all species after at most n rounds. This is species-support logic with all reactants required; it does not replace the complex graph by a species Markov chain.

**Comparison.** Angeli–De Leenheer–Sontag's 2011 paper, Sections 2–7 through both technical proof endings, uses a positive pointwise kinetic envelope and proves that extinction sets are siphons, then excludes them with conserved semiflows. Its proof controls residence near a boundary point using bounded speed and positive inward drift. F1–F4 replace that pointwise step by chronological window propagation and quantify a finite uniform delay. The conserved-siphon mechanism remains the same; this is a technical quantitative PE extension, not a new general boundary mechanism. For an uncovered test family, take the six complexes (2,1,0),(1,2,0),(0,2,1),(0,1,2),(1,0,2),(2,0,1), connected in a bidirectional ring. Total concentration is conserved, and the two independent edge vectors give the open mass-one simplex, of compact closure. The union is weakly reversible. Coordinate vertices are invariant boundary points; for example {B,C} is a critical siphon, so SC does not apply. The rank is two, so Route II does not apply either.

For the general target, F1 controls each flux below by its starting monomial, but its upper effective coefficient can diverge. Production of a rare species can change the monomial hierarchy by an arbitrarily large relative factor in one window. The source's affine minimum can then switch labels. Even if every original reaction appears in a time-discretized step, there is no justified monotonicity of that **continuous** affine minimum: the integral of a changing minimum is not the minimum of fixed-label integrals, and one must control all active branches at ties. Complex graph return paths are not species transfer paths. F2 closes support propagation only when the initial large-species closure reaches everything. A critical siphon can stop that closure. Rank-one ordering supplies an extra power in all harmful terms, but distinct rare coordinates in higher rank need not have one common scalar order. Finite-horizon continuity and compactness do not fill this gap.

The precise unpaid mechanism is uniform repulsion of all accessible critical-siphon faces, including changes among rare-species scales and active labels, under independent PE schedules. Neither a proof nor a counterexample to that exact claim is supplied. The deepest paid new results are F1–F4 and R1–R7. Their complete mechanisms are technical propagation and one-dimensional return estimates; no ninth nomination is forced.

**A tempting anchor retraction fails the norm bound.** Define a(x) on source vertices and fix every anchor. On finite N_m its linearization is a finite-rank operator fixing anchors. For any source edge with different endpoint colors, the endpoint labels are distinct (the own-color coordinate distinguishes them). Distinct anchors have distance at least 2R: a path either uses a direct anchor edge or must leave and reenter the anchor set through two length-R attachments. Therefore this map has norm at least 2R>2p on a molecule of source-edge norm one. Such differently colored edges occur in the actual sequence by the local limit. This rules out the natural low-rank anchor-fixing candidate without treating its label quotient as a degree-Q state graph.
